title: Three shards that move together
subtitle: Cluster, member and phantom vector files are interdependent, so they activate together in one transaction or not at all, only after the files are confirmed on disk, with a single-active invariant the database enforces
technologies: Idempotency, exactly-once effects and crash recovery

stats.label: vector files that activate in one transaction or not at all
active generation per schema and kind, held by a unique index
generations kept so a rollback has somewhere to go

lede: The GPU analytics in Where a cluster sits read three kinds of vector file: the cluster centroids, the members with their per-cluster offsets, and the phantom candidates. The member offsets index into the centroid file, and the phantoms are scored against both. A reader that saw a new centroid file beside an old member file would compute nonsense without an error. So the three files form a coupled set, and the set is the unit of activation. Each kind is built by its own request, and the three requests share a coupled-set identifier. The activation function in the database checks the whole set, and a unique index guards the result.
quote: A partial activation is impossible by construction rather than by convention.
evidence: Transactional artifact management: 3 interdependent vector files activated together in one PostgreSQL transaction or not at all, with a unique index allowing 1 active generation per kind.
Fail-closed artifact pipelines: generations checked on disk before activation, missing as a terminal status, and 2 generations kept so a rollback has somewhere to go.
Deterministic data layout: file names carrying kind and generation, and row order fixed so two builds of the same data are the same bytes, each shard signed with a collision-resistant hash.
author: Corey James
